description: EOS UI/UX Aesthetic Canon -- the canonical design direction, visual identity, design token architecture, and boundary between shared OS platform standards and product-specific aesthetic for EntrepreneurOS.
provenance_detail: Aesthetic direction corrected by operator (executive command center, NOT playful/RPG/creator-social). Design token architecture synthesized from Beast codebase (design-tokens.ts, theme.json), Phase 14.4 desired state (Universal Dashboard Architecture), and professional inference for finance-grade standards. OS platform shared standards synthesized from Phase 14.5 OS Platform Standard v2.

aesthetic_identity.description: EOS looks and feels like the command bridge of a high-performance enterprise. Every element communicates control, clarity, and operational authority. The interface serves operators who manage portfolios, entities, capital flows, and teams -- it must inspire confidence and enable rapid, precise decision-making.
aesthetic_identity.emotional_tone: Authoritative, confident, precise, professional, trustworthy. The operator should feel like they are in control of a sophisticated machine -- not playing a game, not browsing a social feed, not navigating a toy.
ux_metaphor_hierarchy: Primary: Financial terminal / Bloomberg terminal -- dense, information-rich, multi-panel
Secondary: Cockpit / mission control -- status indicators, real-time feeds, action surfaces
Tertiary: Enterprise dashboard -- clean KPI cards, sortable tables, drill-down navigation
reference_products: Bloomberg Terminal (information density, multi-panel layout, real-time data)
Carta (cap table management, finance-grade UX, institutional trust)
Stripe Dashboard (developer-quality precision, clear data hierarchy)
Linear (modern SaaS UX, keyboard shortcuts, fast and precise)
Notion (workspace flexibility -- but NOT the playful aesthetic)
Monday.com (workflow management -- but NOT the colorful/casual aesthetic)

what_eos_is_not_visually.description: Explicit anti-patterns that EOS must never adopt. These exist because three sibling products (LyfeOS, CreatorOS) have different aesthetic directions, and EOS must maintain its distinct identity.

anti_patterns.description: No XP bars, no leveling systems, no achievement badges, no quest metaphors, no RPG-style character sheets. LyfeOS uses these -- EOS does not.
No social feeds, no follower counts, no content engagement metrics as primary UI. CreatorOS uses these -- EOS does not.
No skill trees, no character archetypes, no stat tokens, no energy logs as primary interface elements. EOS is a business operating system, not a self-improvement platform.
No frosted-glass overlays, no heavy blur effects, no translucent cards as primary design language. Finance-grade interfaces prioritize clarity over visual effects.
No bright neon accents, no cyberpunk color schemes, no sci-fi terminal aesthetics. EOS is institutional, not futuristic-theatrical.
No oversized rounded corners, no bouncy animations, no emoji-heavy copy, no playful illustrations. The tone is serious and operational.
No hero sections, no gradient CTAs, no testimonial carousels inside the operating interface. This is an operating system, not a landing page.

design_tokens.description: Design token direction for EOS. These are directional specifications, not final implementation values. Final values will be resolved during implementation.

color_palette.direction: Professional, muted, high-contrast. Finance-grade palette optimized for long working sessions, dense information display, and clear status signaling.

dark_mode.priority: PRIMARY -- EOS operators will work in dark mode by default. Bloomberg, trading terminals, and professional tools default dark.
dark_mode.background_direction: Deep charcoal to near-black (not pure black). Layered surfaces with subtle elevation.
dark_mode.surface_direction: Slightly lighter charcoal for cards, panels, modals. Clear visual hierarchy through surface elevation.
dark_mode.text_direction: High-contrast white/off-white for primary text. Muted gray for secondary. Never low-contrast.
dark_mode.accent_direction: Cool blue primary accent (trust, authority, professionalism). Green for positive/gain. Red for negative/loss/risk. Amber for warning/pending.

light_mode.priority: SECONDARY -- available but not default. Some operators prefer light mode for meetings, presentations, or daytime use.
light_mode.background_direction: Clean white to warm off-white. Not stark hospital-white.
light_mode.surface_direction: Light gray for elevated surfaces. Subtle borders over shadows for card delineation.
light_mode.text_direction: Near-black for primary text. Dark gray for secondary. Clear hierarchy.
light_mode.accent_direction: Same accent colors as dark mode, adjusted for light background contrast.

status_colors.positive_gain_success: Green family -- financial gain, task complete, healthy KPI, approved
status_colors.negative_loss_danger: Red family -- financial loss, overdue, unhealthy KPI, rejected, risk
status_colors.warning_pending_caution: Amber/yellow family -- pending approval, approaching threshold, needs attention
status_colors.inactive_disabled: Muted gray family -- disabled, archived, inactive entity

typography.direction: Professional sans-serif. High legibility at small sizes for dense data displays. Monospace for financial figures.
typography.primary_font_direction: Inter, system-ui, or equivalent modern sans-serif. NOT decorative, NOT serif, NOT handwritten.
typography.monospace_direction: JetBrains Mono, SF Mono, or equivalent for financial figures, KPI values, transaction amounts, code. Tabular numerals required for aligned columns.

scale.xs: Dense data tables, timestamps, secondary metadata (11-12px)
scale.sm: Table cells, form labels, navigation items (13-14px)
scale.xxl: Dashboard hero metrics, portfolio total values (32-48px)

typography.weight_direction: Regular (400) for body. Medium (500) for labels and navigation. Semibold (600) for headings. Bold (700) for KPI values and emphasis. No thin/light weights in data-dense contexts.

spacing.direction: Compact and efficient. Finance-grade interfaces maximize information density without sacrificing readability. NOT generous SaaS whitespace.
spacing.density_model: EOS uses COMPACT density by default. Large whitespace wastes viewport on data-rich screens. Operators need to see more, scroll less.
spacing.grid: 8px base grid. 4px for micro-adjustments. 16px standard gap. 24px section gap. 32px page-level padding.
spacing.table_rows: Compact row height (36-40px) for data tables. Not padded list items (48-56px).

component_style.direction: Sharp, precise, functional. Components communicate data, not decoration.
component_style.border_radius: Small (4-6px) for most elements. Sharp corners for data tables. Slightly larger (8px) for modals and cards. NEVER pill-shaped buttons or fully-rounded cards.
component_style.elevation: Subtle. Use border + slight shadow over heavy drop shadows. Bloomberg-style flat panels over Material Design elevation.
component_style.borders: Visible, thin borders (1px) for structure delineation. Panels, cards, tables all have clear boundaries. NOT borderless floating elements.
component_style.animations: Minimal and fast. No bouncy transitions. No slide-in panels. Instant state changes preferred. Subtle fade (150ms) acceptable for modals.
component_style.icons: Lucide or equivalent clean line icons. NOT filled/solid by default. NOT emoji-style. Consistent stroke width.
component_style.buttons: Solid primary, outline secondary, ghost tertiary. Compact sizing. Clear hover/active states. No gradient buttons.
component_style.tables: First-class citizen. Sortable columns, fixed headers, row selection, inline actions. Dense but readable. Stripe alternate rows in dark mode.
component_style.charts: Recharts or Tremor. Clean axes, muted gridlines, data-focused. No decorative chart elements. Tooltips on hover.

current_code_truth_beast.theme_json_note: Beast has a theme.json file that likely defines base theme values (colors, radii, etc.) for the application. Exact contents not available on VPS -- documented from Beast inventory.

os_platform_standard_shared.description: Technical UX patterns, component discipline, accessibility standards, and interaction standards that are SHARED across all Trinity products (EOS, CreatorOS, LyfeOS). These are the universal platform layer -- every product inherits these, then applies its own aesthetic.

shared_standards.standard: All Trinity products use shadcn/ui as the base component library built on Radix UI primitives. Products customize theme tokens but share the same underlying component API and accessibility guarantees.
Tailwind CSS for all styling. Utility-first. Custom theme tokens injected via tailwind.config.ts. No CSS-in-JS. No separate CSS files except for global resets.
Mobile-responsive layouts. Breakpoints: sm (640px), md (768px), lg (1024px), xl (1280px), 2xl (1536px). Three-panel layout (left rail + workspace + right rail) collapses to single-panel on mobile.
WCAG 2.1 AA minimum. Keyboard navigable. Screen reader compatible (via Radix UI primitives). Color contrast ratios enforced. Focus indicators visible. ARIA labels on interactive elements.

CSS custom properties (variables) for all theme values. Token categories: color, typography, spacing, border, shadow, animation. Tokens defined in tailwind.config.ts and/or design-tokens.ts. Dark/light mode via CSS class toggle.

Toast notifications for async feedback. Confirmation dialogs for destructive actions. Optimistic UI updates where safe. Loading skeletons over spinners. Error boundaries with retry. Form validation on blur + submit.
Three-panel shell: collapsible Left Rail (navigation + context switcher), Main Workspace (content area), collapsible Right Rail (AI assistant). All products share this shell structure.
TanStack Query (React Query) for server state. React context for UI state (theme, rail collapse, active entity). No Redux. No Zustand unless justified.
Client-side routing via wouter (lightweight) or React Router. URL-driven state for bookmarkable views. Route guards for auth and permissions.
Strict TypeScript. Zod for runtime validation of API responses. Drizzle-Zod for schema-derived types. No `any` in production code. Shared types in shared/ directory.

product_specific_aesthetic_boundary.description: Each Trinity product owns its own brand identity, aesthetic, emotional tone, UX metaphor, and visual hierarchy. The shared OS platform standard provides the structural skeleton; the product-specific layer provides the soul.
product_specific_aesthetic_boundary.principle: Products share skeleton, not skin. Same components, different character.

eos_owns: Chart theming and data visualization approach
os_platform_standard_owns: Three-panel shell structure (left rail + workspace + right rail)

sibling_comparison.aesthetic: RPG life operating system / gamified personal development
sibling_comparison.ux_metaphor: Character sheet, quest log, skill tree
Studio workspace, content calendar, audience dashboard

layout_architecture.description: EOS shell layout architecture -- the structural skeleton that all EOS screens share.

shell_components.content: Portfolio/entity switcher at top, role-dependent navigation tree below, settings/profile at bottom
shell_components.behavior: Collapsible via toggle or hotkey. Remembers state. Shows entity context at all times.

shell_components.content: Context-dependent: dashboards, tables, forms, boards, org charts, workflow views, document editors
shell_components.behavior: Full-width when both rails collapsed. Scrollable content area. Breadcrumb navigation at top.

shell_components.content: Contextual AI interface: EA or context-appropriate agent. Shows recommendations, risks, explanations, suggested actions relevant to current workspace view.
shell_components.behavior: Collapsible. Context-aware -- changes content based on current page/entity/selection. Chat input at bottom.

shell_components.content: Global search, notification bell, user avatar, entity context breadcrumb, quick-action triggers
Quick command input, agent status indicator, expand to full command palette. Ask EA, generate business, generate entity, create workflow, assign task.
shell_components.behavior: Always visible. Expands on click/hotkey. Collapses after action. Does not block workspace content.

shell_components.position: Inline within workspace or as banner below header
shell_components.content: Pending approvals, unsafe action warnings, permission conflicts, business risks, compliance alerts, agent autonomy escalation requests
shell_components.behavior: Contextual -- only appears when relevant. Dismissible after action. Persists until resolved for critical items.

shell_components.position: Tab within Right Rail or dedicated panel
shell_components.content: Real-time stream: human actions, agent actions, workflow executions, approvals, comments, system events, KPI changes, decisions
shell_components.behavior: Filterable by type (human, agent, system). Chronological. Linkable entries. Auto-updates.

data_visualization_standards.description: Standards for how EOS displays financial, operational, and strategic data.

kpi_display.format: Hero metric cards with label, current value, trend indicator (up/down/flat), change amount, change percentage, sparkline
kpi_display.currency: Locale-aware formatting. Monospace/tabular numerals for alignment.
kpi_display.comparison: Period-over-period comparison (vs last week, month, quarter, year). Color-coded change (green positive, red negative).

tables.default: Dense data tables with sortable columns, fixed header, row hover, row selection, inline actions
tables.financial_tables: Right-aligned numbers. Tabular numerals. Thousand separators. Negative values in red or parentheses.

charts.library_direction: Recharts or Tremor (both React-native, composable, shadcn-compatible)
charts.style: Clean, data-focused. Muted gridlines. Clear axes. Tooltips on hover. No decorative elements. Consistent color coding with status colors.

keyboard_and_power_user.description: EOS targets power users who operate their businesses daily. Keyboard shortcuts and command palette are first-class features.

command_palette.capabilities: Navigate to any page, switch entity, search entities/tasks/workflows, trigger actions, invoke EA commands

examples: G then D: Go to dashboard
G then T: Go to tasks
G then W: Go to workflows

open_questions.question: Should EOS enforce dark mode only for initial launch, or ship with both dark and light from day one?
open_questions.recommendation: Ship both, default to dark. Many operators will present to stakeholders in light mode.

open_questions.question: Should the Beast design-tokens.ts values be preserved as-is, or should they be replaced with the finance-grade direction described here?
open_questions.recommendation: Audit Beast tokens against this spec during implementation. Preserve compatible values, update divergent ones.

open_questions.question: Should EOS adopt a specific commercial font (e.g., Inter, Geist) or stay with system fonts?
open_questions.recommendation: Inter -- free, professional, excellent tabular numerals, widely used in finance/enterprise SaaS.

open_questions.question: What level of information density should the default dashboard target? Bloomberg-level (extreme density) vs Stripe-level (balanced density)?
open_questions.recommendation: Stripe-level as default with operator option to increase density. Bloomberg-level is overwhelming for most operators.

open_questions.question: Should the Activity/Event Feed live as a tab in the Right Rail or as a separate expandable panel?
open_questions.recommendation: Tab in Right Rail (switch between AI Assistant and Activity Feed). Avoids adding more shell chrome.

implementation_debt.description: Beast branch has no documented design system. design-tokens.ts exists but no design spec or Storybook.
No component documentation or Storybook for Beast UI components.
No dark mode implementation verified in Beast. theme.json exists but dark mode behavior unconfirmed.
No accessibility audit has been performed on either GitHub main or Beast branch.
No keyboard shortcuts or command palette implemented in Beast.
